title: Flock Safety
because: OUI {prefix} is registered to {org} in the IEEE MA-L registry. That block belongs to Flock Safety, which builds automated license-plate cameras.

title: Flock list, module vendor
because: OUI {prefix} is registered to {org}. ESP32 Marauder v1.21.0 includes this prefix in WiFiScan.cpp oui_list, and DeFlock community lists use the same style of module OUI. The IEEE registrant is not Flock Safety, so this is a lead shared with a lot of ordinary radios.

title: Flock setup SSID
because: SSID "{ssid}" matches the Flock-XXXXXX name documented from Falcon camera beacons.
proberBecause: This station probed for "{ssid}", a Flock-style SSID. A probe shows a searched or remembered name, not that this radio is a Flock camera.

sources.title: Ryan O'Horo, Spotting Flock Safety's Falcon Cameras

title: Flock test_flck SSID
because: SSID "{ssid}" is the development name DeFlock and WatchFlock report as baked into Flock camera firmware.
proberBecause: This station probed for "{ssid}". That is the development SSID associated with Flock firmware, not proof this radio is the camera.

title: SSID Flock
because: SSID "{ssid}" is exactly Flock. The match is the whole name, so a network such as Flockhart does not qualify.
proberBecause: This station probed for the SSID "{ssid}".

title: Flock BLE name
because: Advertisement carries XUNTONG company ID 0x09C8 and a name ({name}) that ESP32 Marauder treats as a Flock camera in isFlockCamera().

title: Genetec
because: OUI {prefix} is registered to {org}. Genetec sells the AutoVu license-plate platform and other security products, so the block identifies the vendor rather than one camera model. The separate IEEE entry "GENETEC Corporation" is not included.

title: Motorola Solutions

match.pattern: ^Motorola Solutions Inc\.$|^MOTOROLA SOLUTIONS MALAYSIA SDN\. BHD\.$

because: OUI {prefix} is registered to {org}. Motorola Solutions absorbed Vigilant Solutions, an ALPR vendor, and also ships radios and other public-safety gear. The OUI is the vendor, not proof of a plate reader.

title: Hikvision
because: OUI {prefix} is registered to {org}. Hikvision's blocks cover cameras and recorders, so this identifies the manufacturer.

title: Dahua
because: OUI {prefix} is registered to {org}. Dahua's blocks cover cameras and recorders, so this identifies the manufacturer.

title: Wyze
because: OUI {prefix} is registered to {org}. Wyze Labs registrations are the company's own blocks.

title: Ring
because: OUI {prefix} is registered to {org}. Ring LLC's MA-L blocks are the company's own. Names that merely contain "ring" are not matched.

title: Arlo
because: OUI {prefix} is registered to {org}. Only the Arlo Technology blocks are matched. Arlotto and Carlo Gavazzi are different registrants and are not.

title: Axis
because: OUI {prefix} is registered to {org}, the camera company.

title: Hikvision SSID
because: SSID "{ssid}" contains Hikvision as a whole word.

title: Dahua SSID
because: SSID "{ssid}" contains Dahua as a whole word.

title: Wyze SSID
because: SSID "{ssid}" starts with Wyze.

title: Ring SSID
because: SSID "{ssid}" matches the Ring- prefix used by Ring setup networks. A word that merely contains "ring" does not.

title: Arlo SSID
because: SSID "{ssid}" starts with Arlo.

title: Axis SSID
because: SSID "{ssid}" starts with Axis.

title: WiFi Pineapple SSID
because: SSID "{ssid}" matches the Pineapple_ plus four hex digits management name used by Hak5 WiFi Pineapple Mark-series gear. The Pineapple Pager does not have a published unique SSID: Hak5's own PineAP notes say it advertises a pool of arbitrary names and can randomize the BSSID.
proberBecause: This station probed for "{ssid}", a Pineapple-style management SSID. Probing for it is not the same as being the Pineapple.

title: Hak5-style local MAC
because: MAC prefix {prefix} is one of the locally administered addresses ESP32 Marauder lists under Hak5 in its pine-scan table. Hak5 has no IEEE registration. The same addresses can be set by anyone, and the Pineapple Pager can randomize its BSSID, so this is a hint about Hak5-style gear rather than a specific model.

title: Alfa radio
because: OUI {prefix} is registered to {org}. ESP32 Marauder marks Alfa as suspicious when the AP is open because some WiFi Pineapple hardware used Alfa radios. The registry entry is Alfa, not Hak5.

title: Orient Power radio
because: OUI {prefix} is registered to {org}. ESP32 Marauder comments this block as Orient Power hardware used in the WiFi Pineapple Mark VII. The registry entry is Orient Power, not Hak5.

title: Deauther SSID
because: SSID "{ssid}" matches the default control-network name used by the ESP8266 Deauther project.
proberBecause: This station probed for "{ssid}", the default ESP8266 Deauther SSID.

title: Deauther name
because: SSID "{ssid}" contains deauther as a whole word.

title: Pwnagotchi name
because: SSID "{ssid}" contains pwnagotchi. The stronger signature is the beacon vendor element whose JSON includes the key pwnd_tot. RCN1 does not store beacon bodies, so that check runs only when a beacon text supplement is present.

title: Pwnagotchi beacon
because: Beacon text contains pwnd_tot, the handshake counter a pwnagotchi puts in its vendor information element. ESP32 Marauder detects other pwnagotchis the same way.

title: Marauder name
because: SSID "{ssid}" starts with Marauder. The firmware does not advertise a fixed SSID during Recon, so this is only a name match.

title: ESP32 deauth activity
because: This MAC transmitted {count} deauthentication frame(s), and OUI {prefix} is registered to {org}. That fits an ESP32 Marauder or a deauther board. It also fits any other ESP32 that sent those frames. An Espressif OUI with no deauth is not flagged.

title: Deauth frames
because: This MAC transmitted {count} deauthentication frame(s) recorded as obs.rlog type d. The log shows the activity. It does not name the tool.

title: Flipper Zero
because: BLE service UUID {service} is one of 0x3081, 0x3082, and 0x3083. ESP32 Marauder maps those to Flipper Zero case colors (black, white, transparent). The advertisement carries the UUID little-endian, so the bytes on air are 81 30, 82 30, or 83 30.

title: Flipper name
because: Advertised name "{name}" starts with Flipper. Owners can rename the device, and other products can copy the name, so this is weaker than the service UUID.

title: Flipper Devices OUI
because: OUI {prefix} is registered to {org}. This Wi-Fi block is not how a Flipper Zero is identified. The Zero is matched by BLE service UUIDs 0x3081–0x3083. The same OUI has been reported on Flipper's BUSY Bar.

title: Ray-Ban Meta glasses
because: The advertisement names "{name}" and includes Meta service UUID 0xFD5F. ESP32 Marauder lists 0xFD5F as a Meta identifier. The name makes the glasses reading specific. A phone running a Meta app can advertise 0xFD5F without that name.

title: Meta service UUID
because: Service UUID {service} is 0xFD5F, which ESP32 Marauder lists as Meta. Ray-Ban Meta glasses advertise it. Phones running Meta apps can advertise it too, so the UUID alone is not the glasses.

title: Glasses name
because: Advertised name "{name}" matches a Ray-Ban Meta, Oakley Meta, or Meta Ray-Ban display name. Names can be copied.

title: Luxottica company ID
because: Manufacturer data uses company ID 0x0D53, which ESP32 Marauder labels as Luxottica, the Ray-Ban parent. Other Luxottica products can use it.

title: Meta company ID
because: Manufacturer data uses a Meta Platforms company ID ({company}). ESP32 Marauder lists 0x01AB and 0x058E as Meta. Quest headsets and other Meta radios share them, so this is not specifically glasses.

title: Apple Find My
because: Manufacturer data contains Apple company ID 0x004C followed by Find My type 0x12. ESP32 Marauder classifies that as FindMy. AirTags use it once they are participating in offline finding. Other Find My accessories use it too. Company ID 0x004C alone is not matched, because ordinary Apple radios share it.

sources.title: Heinrich, Stute, Kornhuber, Hollick. Who Can Find My Devices? arXiv:2103.02282

title: Find My network accessory
because: Service UUID {service} is 0xFD44, the Find My Network Accessory service ESP32 Marauder uses when separating AirTags from other Find My radios.

title: Unwanted-tracker service
because: Advertisement includes the Detecting Unwanted Location Trackers service UUID that ESP32 Marauder records for Find My accessories.

title: Tile tracker
because: Service UUID {service} is a 16-bit UUID the Bluetooth SIG assigns to Tile, Inc. (0xFEED and 0xFEEC).

title: Samsung SmartTag
because: Service UUID {service} is 0xFD5A. The Bluetooth SIG assigns that 16-bit UUID to Samsung, and the SmartTag discovery protocol uses it. ESP32 Marauder lists 0xFD5A as a Samsung identifier and does not treat it as Meta.

title: iBeacon
because: obs.rlog type {raw} is an iBeacon. Firmware writes 'i' for a new iBeacon and 'I' for a repeat only after parseIBeacon accepts the advertisement. The 21-byte RCN1 record does not contain the UUID, major, minor, or measured power. Those stay in device RAM on v1.21.0 unless a supplement carries the manufacturer data.

title: iBeacon payload
because: Bytes match Apple's iBeacon header 4C 00 02 15. UUID {uuid}, major {major}, minor {minor}, measured power {tx} dBm.

title: Locally administered MAC
because: The U/L bit (bit 1 of the first octet) is set, so this is a locally administered address as defined by IEEE 802. Phones use that bit for MAC randomization. Spoofed interfaces, virtual machines, and some Hak5 radios use it too. There is no universal OUI to look up.

sources.title: IEEE registration authority, OUI and MAC address structure
